newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Italy backs Slovenia NATO, EU bids - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy backs Slovenia NATO, EU bids - Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday Italy strongly supported Slovenia's bid to join NATO and the European Union in the first round of their expansion.
"Italy strongly supports Slovenia's joining the first group of countries that will expand NATO and the EU," Prodi told a news conference during his first official visit to Ljubljana.

Slovenia hopes to be invited to start negotiations on full membership of NATO at the alliance summit in Madrid on July 7 and 8, and to become a full member in 1999, while it aims for full EU membership by 2001.
"In the next months a mixed Italian-Slovenian group will be established that will work on bilateral questions so that all shadows of the past will disappear," Prodi said.

Relations between Slovenia and Italy have greatly improved since April last year when Prodi came to power. Prior to that, Italy blocked Slovenia's EU association agreement because Slovenia refused to hand back property confiscated from ethnic Italians after World War Two.

Slovenia's association agreement with the EU was signed two months after Prodi came to power and is expected to be ratified by Slovenian and all EU member governments later this year. Italy is Slovenia's second major trading partner, accounting for about 20 percent of its foreign trade.
